finding: the closing procedure told me to run a script that starts a new 24-hour stress run
howItSurfaced: Checking the TestRoot trap before closing time. Reading tools/Test-S5Stress.ps1 rather than recalling what it does showed it is not the verifier I had recorded.

whatTheScriptActuallyDoes.parameters: TestRoot, Seed 9282026, Profile vanilla, Hours 24, Concurrency 8
whatTheScriptActuallyDoes.behaviour: It builds gradlew runS5Stress arguments with -PgreatwallStressHours and -PgreatwallStressMinutes from Hours, starts the process, and blocks reading its stdout and stderr until it ends
whatTheScriptActuallyDoes.thenItJudges: passed = code -eq 0 and not timeout and report.passed -eq true, reading the newest stress-report.json under <root>/build/stress-reports

whyThatIsWrongAtClosingTime.itWouldStartASecond24HourRun: With the default Hours of 24, invoking it after the current profile ends would begin another full-length profile
whyThatIsWrongAtClosingTime.itWouldContend: It runs gradlew, so it would also compete with whatever else is running
whyThatIsWrongAtClosingTime.theRecordedCommandWasWrong: The procedure's step5StressVerdict named this script, which read correctly as a verification step but is a launcher

whatReplacesIt: Read the report the finished profile wrote, under build/run/serverSmoke/vanilla/s5stress24h20261007084723/build/stress-reports/run-*/stress-report.json, and apply the same rule the script applies: passed needs passed==true and durationMet==true, because StressFixture halts with server.halt(false) and so exits 0 even when the profile failed.
theScriptsRemainingValue: Its pass rule and its refusal to trust an exit code are the parts worth reusing; only its launching behaviour disqualifies it here.
theTestRootTrapIsStillRecorded: If it is ever run deliberately, the root must include serverSmoke\vanilla and sit under build\run. A path like build\run\s5stress24h20261007084723 passes the guard but holds no stress-reports directory, giving a fail-closed passed=false that looks like a profile failure.
